feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iteration 4 (50 mm span, 12 mm footprint, y 0.05) gave oval progress 0.710. Iteration 0 (40 mm) gave 0.664 and iteration 3 (60 mm, 12 mm) gave 0.275, so the 50 mm span is near the best and should stay. Iteration 1 (y 0.03) collapsed oval progress to 0.273, so keep y 0.05. Iteration 5 (base 1.3, kd 0.40) lifted oval progress to 0.884 and cut oval max_error to 0.046 m, but s-bend and slalom max_error stayed at 0.0625 and 0.0647 m. Decide from the next race as follows. If s-bend and slalom max_error falls below about 0.06 m with oval progress at 0.65 or more, keep the geometry and tune the controller further. If s-bend or slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 m while oval progress holds, the excursions are not speed-limited, so test wheel_track 0.10 in the following iteration with no other geometry change, as requested below. If oval progress drops below about 0.65 because the robot is too slow, the controller speed change is the cause, not the geometry, so keep the span and restore base_speed.
requested_changes: If s-bend and slalom max_error is still at or above 0.06 m while oval progress is at or above 0.65, change wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 with no other geometry change. Iterations 0 to 5 show max_error on its plateau (0.059 to 0.065 m) across every span, footprint and lead, so turn rate is the untested lever.

Keep sensor_positions at x = -0.025, -0.0125, 0, 0.0125, 0.025 with y 0.05 and sensor_size 0.012. Iteration 4 (50 mm, 12 mm, y 0.05) reached oval progress 0.710 with line losses of 1.0 to 1.4, and iteration 1 showed that y 0.03 cuts oval progress to 0.273.
Do not change the span to 40 mm in the next iteration. Iteration 0 (40 mm) gave oval progress 0.664, below the 0.710 at 50 mm, so narrowing the span is not supported by the evidence.
